They disagreed and disputed concerning the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ) and what he had brought them. ﴿About the momentous news,﴾ Mujahid said it is the Qur'an, citing as evidence His saying: ﴿Say: It is a momentous news.﴾ [[Qur'an 38:67.]] Qatada said it is the Resurrection. ﴿About which they differ.﴾ Some affirm it and some deny it. ﴿No! They will come to know.﴾ ﴿Again, no! They will come to know.﴾ This is a warning to them. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿No! They will come to know﴾ refers to the disbelievers, and ﴿again, no! They will come to know﴾ refers to the believers. The reading of the majority (al-ʿAmma, the common readers) is with the yāʾ in both places, while al-Hasan and Malik ibn Dinar read with the tāʾ in both places.

﴿Have We not made the earth a resting-place,﴾ ﴿and the mountains as pegs,﴾ ﴿and created you in pairs,﴾ meaning kinds: males and females.

﴿And We made your sleep a rest﴾ (subat), a repose for your bodies. The sleeper is ʾmasbūt,ʾ one who does not know or perceive, as if he were dead. ﴿And We made the night a covering,﴾ a cover and veil, which clothes everything with its darkness. ﴿And We made the day a means of livelihood,﴾ a cause of your sustenance and of attending to your affairs. He named it thus, as in the saying of the poet:

"The one afflicted with worries, when worries gather around him, [the darkness of] night is his pillow, and he does not sleep."

Thus he made the pillow the thing that does not sleep, while the meaning refers to the owner of the pillow.

﴿And We built above you seven strong ones,﴾ ﴿and We made a blazing lamp,﴾ meaning shining, luminous, burning, hot, which is the sun. ﴿And We sent down from the rain-laden clouds﴾ (al-muʿṣirāt). Mujahid, Muqatil and Qatada said: it means the winds that squeeze the clouds, and this is the narration of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas. On this interpretation, the min in "min al-muʿṣirāt" means "bi" (with), as in His saying: ﴿from every matter, peace﴾ [[Qur'an 97:4–5.]]. ʿIkrima used to read it as "wa-anzalnā bil-muʿṣirāt." Al-Aʿmash narrated from al-Minhal, from Ibn ʿAmr, and from Qays ibn Sakan, who said: ʿAbd Allah said concerning His saying ﴿and We sent down from the rain-laden clouds water pouring forth﴾: Allah sent the wind, which carried water from the water, so it swelled as a she-camel's milk swells, then He sent the water like great waterskins, and the winds strike it so that it falls scattered. [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi: 3/364.]]

The historian said: al-muʿṣirāt means "those possessing whirlwinds" (dhawāt al-aʿāṣīr). Abu al-ʿAliya, al-Rabiʿ and al-Dahhak said: they are the clouds which bring rain but have not yet rained, like a woman who is "muʿṣir," whose menstruation is near. Abu al-Najm said:

"She has begun to menstruate, or her time of it has drawn near."

This is also the narration of al-Wali from Ibn ʿAbbas. Al-Mubarrad said: al-muʿṣirāt means "al-fāṭirāt" (those that split open). Ibn Kaysan said: "al-mughīthāt" (those that bring relief), from His saying ﴿they are pressed﴾ [[Qur'an 12:49.]]. Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, al-Hasan, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Zayd ibn Aslam and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: ﴿from the rain-laden clouds﴾ means from the heavens.

﴿Water pouring forth﴾ means pouring abundantly. Mujahid said: "abundant." Qatada said: "in succession, one following another." Ibn Zayd said: "much."

﴿That We may bring forth thereby grain and plants,﴾ ﴿and gardens of entwined growth,﴾ meaning gathered and intertwined, one part joined with another. Its singular, according to the grammarians of Basra, is "alaff," though this view is not strong; according to others its singular is "laff" and "lafif." It is also said that it is a plural of a plural: one says "jannah lafā" and "bint lafā" and "jinān lafā" (with the lām vowelled with a ḍammah), and then "lafā" is pluralized as "alfāf."

Ibn Fanjawayh told me: Ibn Shanbah told us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Kisa'i told us: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar told us: Muhammad ibn Zuhayr told us, from Muhammad ibn al-Muhtadi, from Hanzala al-Dawri, from his father, from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib, who said: Muʿadh ibn Jabal was sitting near the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the house of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari. Muʿadh said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿The Day the Trumpet is blown, and you will come forth in throngs﴾?" He said: "Muʿadh, you have asked about a grave matter." Then he let his eyes fall, and then said: "You will be gathered in ten kinds from among my community, scattered groups. Allah, the Exalted, has separated them from the congregation of the Muslims and changed their forms. Some of them are in the forms of monkeys, some in the form of pigs, some are upside down, with their feet above and their faces below, dragged upon them. Some are blind, wandering about; some are deaf and mute, who do not understand. Some chew their tongues while they hang upon their chests, and pus flows from their mouths, which the people of the gathering find disgusting. Some have their hands and feet cut off. Some are crucified on trunks of fire. Some are more foul-smelling than carrion. Some wear garments of tar, sticking to their skins. Those crucified on trunks of fire are those who inform on people to the authorities. Those more foul than carrion are those who indulge in desires and pleasures and withhold the right of Allah, the Exalted, from their wealth. Those who wear the garments are the people of arrogance, pride and vanity."" [86] [[Al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/307.]]

﴿And We built above you seven strong ones,﴾ ﴿and We made a blazing lamp,﴾ meaning shining, luminous, burning, hot, which is the sun. ﴿And We sent down from the rain-laden clouds﴾ (al-muʿṣirāt). On this interpretation, the min in "min al-muʿṣirāt" means "bi" (with), as in His saying: ﴿from every matter, peace﴾ [[Qur'an 97:4–5.]]. ʿIkrima used to read it as "wa-anzalnā bil-muʿṣirāt." Al-Aʿmash narrated from al-Minhal, from Ibn ʿAmr, and from Qays ibn Sakan, who said: ʿAbd Allah said concerning His saying ﴿and We sent down from the rain-laden clouds water pouring forth﴾: Allah sent the wind, which carried water from the water, so it swelled as a she-camel's milk swells, then He sent the water like great waterskins, and the winds strike it so that it falls scattered. [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi: 3/364.]]

The historian said: al-muʿṣirāt means "those possessing whirlwinds" (dhawāt al-aʿāṣīr). Abu al-ʿAliya, al-Rabiʿ and al-Dahhak said: they are the clouds which bring rain but have not yet rained, like a woman who is "muʿṣir," whose menstruation is near. Abu al-Najm said:

"She has begun to menstruate, or her time of it has drawn near."

This is also the narration of al-Wali from Ibn ʿAbbas. Al-Mubarrad said: al-muʿṣirāt means "al-fāṭirāt" (those that split open). Ibn Kaysan said: "al-mughīthāt" (those that bring relief), from His saying ﴿they are pressed﴾ [[Qur'an 12:49.]]. Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, al-Hasan, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Zayd ibn Aslam and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: ﴿from the rain-laden clouds﴾ means from the heavens.

﴿Water pouring forth﴾ means pouring abundantly. Mujahid said: "abundant." Qatada said: "in succession, one following another." Ibn Zayd said: "much."

﴿That We may bring forth thereby grain and plants,﴾ ﴿and gardens of entwined growth,﴾ meaning gathered and intertwined, one part joined with another. Its singular, according to the grammarians of Basra, is "alaff," though this view is not strong; according to others its singular is "laff" and "lafif." It is also said that it is a plural of a plural: one says "jannah lafā" and "bint lafā" and "jinān lafā" (with the lām vowelled with a ḍammah), and then "lafā" is pluralized as "alfāf."

﴿Indeed, the Day of Decision is a fixed time,﴾ as Allah, glorified is He, promised. ﴿The Day the Trumpet is blown, and you will come forth in throngs﴾ [...] [[An illegible word in the manuscript.]],

Ibn Fanjawayh told me: Ibn Shanbah told us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Kisa'i told us: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar told us: Muhammad ibn Zuhayr told us, from Muhammad ibn al-Muhtadi, from Hanzala al-Dawri, from his father, from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib, who said: Muʿadh ibn Jabal was sitting near the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the house of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari. Muʿadh said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿The Day the Trumpet is blown, and you will come forth in throngs﴾?" He said: "Muʿadh, you have asked about a grave matter." Then he let his eyes fall, and then said: "You will be gathered in ten kinds from among my community, scattered groups. Allah, the Exalted, has separated them from the congregation of the Muslims and changed their forms. Some of them are in the forms of monkeys, some in the form of pigs, some are upside down, with their feet above and their faces below, dragged upon them. Some are blind, wandering about; some are deaf and mute, who do not understand. Some chew their tongues while they hang upon their chests, and pus flows from their mouths, which the people of the gathering find disgusting. Some have their hands and feet cut off. Some are crucified on trunks of fire. Some are more foul-smelling than carrion. Some wear garments of tar, sticking to their skins. As for those in the form of monkeys, they are the tale-bearers among people, meaning the slanderers. Those in the form of pigs are those who consume forbidden gain. Those who are upside down with their faces down are the consumers of usury. The blind are those who act unjustly in judgment. The deaf and mute are those who are self-admiring in their deeds. Those who chew their tongues are the scholars and storytellers whose words contradicted their deeds. Those whose hands and feet are cut off are those who harm their neighbors. Those crucified on trunks of fire are those who inform on people to the authorities. Those more foul than carrion are those who indulge in desires and pleasures and withhold the right of Allah, the Exalted, from their wealth. Those who wear the garments are the people of arrogance, pride and vanity."" [86] [[Al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/307.]]

﴿And the sky will be opened,﴾ the people of Kufa read it with the lightened form (takhfif), and others with the intensified form (tashdid). ﴿And it will become gates,﴾ meaning it will be split open for the descent of the angels. It is also said: it will be split until it becomes like gates in pieces. It is also said: it will dissolve and scatter until gates and paths appear in it. It is also said: every servant has two doors in the heaven: a door for his deeds and a door for his provision. When the Resurrection comes, the doors will be opened.

﴿And the mountains will be set in motion﴾ away from the surface of the earth, ﴿and they will become a mirage,﴾ like a mirage. ﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever-lying in wait,﴾ a path and a passage, so there is no way to Paradise until one passes through the Fire. Muqatil said: a place of confinement. ﴿For the transgressors, a place of return,﴾ for the disbelievers. ﴿Abiding therein for ages﴾ (lābithīna). The majority read it with an alif, while ʿAlqama and Hamza read it as "labithīn" without the alif, and both are dialectal forms. ﴿Therein, ages (aḥqāban)﴾, the plural of "ḥuqb," and "ḥuqb" is the plural of "ḥuqba," as in the saying of Mutammim:

"We were like the boon companions of Judhayma for an age of time, until it was said they would never separate."

The scholars differed concerning the meaning of ḥuqb. Some said it is a term for a period of time and an age, without a fixed limit. Abu al-Duha narrated from Ibn Masʿud, who said: "No one knows the number of the ages except Allah, Mighty and Majestic." Others said it has a limit. Then they differed about the length of its duration. Tariq ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman said: An old man called me between al-Safa and al-Marwa, and with him was a book of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr: "Abiding therein for ages"; a ḥuqb is eighty years, each day of which is a thousand years.

Ibn Fanjawayh told me: Musa ibn Muhammad and Ibn Hasan told us: Muhammad ibn ʿImran told us: Ibn al-Muqri and Abu ʿUbayd Allah told us: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-ʿUrni told us, from Sufyan, from ʿAmmar al-Dahni, who said: ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said to Hilal al-Hajari: "What do they find concerning the ḥuqb in the revealed Book of Allah?" He said: "He finds in the Book of Allah eighty years, each year twelve months, each month thirty days, each day a thousand years."

Ibn Fanjawayh told me: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fatḥ told us: Abu Hamid Muhammad ibn Harun al-Hadrami told us: Ziyad ibn Abi Yazid told us: Sulayman ibn Muslim told us, from Sulayman al-Hatmi, from Nafiʿ, from [Ibn ʿUmar], from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "By Allah, no one who enters the Fire will leave it until they have remained in it for ages. A ḥuqb is eighty-some years, and a year is three hundred and sixty days, each day a thousand years, of what you count." So let no one rely on the hope that he will leave the Fire. [87] [[Al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/308.]]

Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: It has reached me that a ḥuqb is three hundred years, each year three hundred and sixty days, each day a thousand years. Al-Hasan said: Allah, glorified is He, has not mentioned anything without making for it a term at which it ends, but He did not make a term for the people of the Fire. Rather He said: ﴿abiding therein for ages.﴾ By Allah, it is only that when one age passes, another begins, then another, and another, and so on to everlasting eternity. There is no number for the ages except eternal abiding in the Fire. But they have mentioned that one ḥuqb is seventy thousand years, each day of which is a thousand years of what we count. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: one ḥuqb is seventeen thousand years. He said: this verse is abrogated by ﴿so We will increase you only in punishment﴾ [[Qur'an 78:30.]], meaning that the count has ended and eternity has been attained. Some scholars said the meaning of the verse ﴿abiding therein for ages﴾ is: they will not taste during those ages anything except boiling water and ghassaq, and then they will remain for ages tasting the heat of the boiling water. Ghassaq is among the kinds of punishment. Thus it is a specification of kinds of punishment, not a specification of their staying in the Fire.

﴿They will not taste therein any coolness﴾ that would cool them from the heat, ﴿except boiling water and ghassaq﴾, which is zamharir (extreme cold). It is also said: the pus of the people of the blaze. al-Thumali said: their tears. Shahr ibn Hawshab said: ghassaq is a valley in the Fire, containing three hundred and thirty ravines, each ravine containing three hundred and thirty houses, each house having four corners, and in each corner a serpent greater than the greatest creature Allah has created, and on the head of each serpent is poison.

﴿Nor any drink that quenches,﴾ from thirst, ﴿except boiling water.﴾ ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid told me: Hamid ibn Muhammad told us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hammad told us: Muhammad ibn ʿAli al-Hasan al-Shaqiqi told us: I asked Abu Muʿadh al-Nahwi, al-Fadl ibn Khalid al-Marwazi, about His saying: ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness﴾, and he said: "The coolness (barad) is sleep." Al-Kisa'i and Abu ʿUbayda said the same, and they recited concerning it:

"Its lips grew cool upon me, so it turned me away from it, and from its kisses the coolness."

The Arabs say: "The coolness prevented the coolness," meaning sleep removed the coolness. Al-Farra' said: sleep does indeed cool its owner, and the thirsty one sleeps and his thirst is cooled, so sleep is called "barad" for this reason. A poet said:

"If you wish, I will forbid women other than you, and if you wish, I will not taste sweet cool water, nor coolness."

Al-Hasan and ʿAta' said: ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness﴾ means refreshment and rest.

﴿As a recompense﴾ is in the accusative as an infinitive; its meaning is: We recompensed them with a recompense.

﴿Fitting (wifāqan)﴾, suited to their deeds as a fitting measure, as we say: "He fought a fight (qatal)," according to al-Akhfash. al-Farra' said: it is the plural of "wafq," and "wafq" and "lafq" are the same. al-Rabiʿ said: a recompense according to their deeds. al-Dahhak said: according to the measure of their deeds. Muqatil said: the punishment matched the sin, for there is no sin greater than polytheism and no punishment greater than the Fire. al-Hasan and ʿIkrima said: their deeds were evil, so Allah recompensed them with what would grieve them.

﴿Indeed they did not expect a reckoning,﴾ meaning they did not fear accountability. ﴿And they denied Our signs with complete denial.﴾ al-Farra' said: this is an eloquent Yemeni dialect; they say: "kadhdhaba kidhdhāban" (he denied with denial), and "kharraqtu al-qamīṣa kharrāqan" (I tore the shirt into tearing). In their dialect, every form of "fa''ala" has the masdar "fa''āl" with the doubled consonant. He said: a Bedouin of them said to me: "ʿAlayya al-marwa, tastaftīnī al-ḥallāq ahabb ilayka am al-qaṣṣāb?" (Upon me is the marwa; will you ask me whether the barber or the butcher is more beloved to you?). And some of the Banu Kilab recited to me:

"Indeed, it has long hindered me from my companion, and from a need whose fulfillment is from our healing."

﴿And We have enumerated everything in a Book.﴾ ﴿So taste; for We will increase you only in punishment.﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh told me:

al-Sunni told us. He said: Ibn Manjawayh informed me: Abu Dawud al-Harrani told us: Shuʿayb ibn Hayyan told us: Mahdi ibn Maymun told us: I heard al-Hasan ibn Dinar ask al-Hasan about the most severe verse in the Qur'an for the people of the Fire. Al-Hasan said: I asked Abu Barza al-Aslami, and he said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said:

"﴿So taste; for We will increase you only in punishment.﴾"

Makkan. It has 770 letters, 173 words, and 40 verses.

Ibn al-Mu'azzi told me: Ibn Mutarriz told us: Ibn Shurayk told us: Ibn Yunus told us: Sallam told us: Harun ibn Kathir told us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, from Abu Umamah, from Ubayy, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites ʿAmma yatasaʾalun (78), Allah, glorified and exalted is He, will give him to drink of the cool drink on the Day of Resurrection." [85] [[Tafsir Majmaʿ al-Bayan: 10/237.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿About what are they asking each other?﴾ That is, about what are these polytheists asking one another? They disagreed and disputed concerning the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ) and what he had brought them. ﴿About the momentous news,﴾ Mujahid said it is the Qur'an, citing as evidence His saying: ﴿Say: It is a momentous news.﴾ [[Qur'an 38:67.]] Qatada said it is the Resurrection. ﴿About which they differ.﴾ Some affirm it and some deny it. ﴿No! They will come to know.﴾ ﴿Again, no! They will come to know.﴾ This is a warning to them. Al-Dahhak said: ﴿No! They will come to know﴾ refers to the disbelievers, and ﴿again, no! They will come to know﴾ refers to the believers. The reading of the majority (al-ʿAmma, the common readers) is with the yāʾ in both places, while al-Hasan and Malik ibn Dinar read with the tāʾ in both places.

﴿Have We not made the earth a resting-place,﴾ ﴿and the mountains as pegs,﴾ ﴿and created you in pairs,﴾ meaning kinds: males and females.

﴿And We made your sleep a rest﴾ (subat), a repose for your bodies. The sleeper is ʾmasbūt,ʾ one who does not know or perceive, as if he were dead. ﴿And We made the night a covering,﴾ a cover and veil, which clothes everything with its darkness. ﴿And We made the day a means of livelihood,﴾ a cause of your sustenance and of attending to your affairs. "The one afflicted with worries, when worries gather around him, [the darkness of] night is his pillow, and he does not sleep."

Thus he made the pillow the thing that does not sleep, while the meaning refers to the owner of the pillow.

﴿Indeed they did not expect a reckoning,﴾ meaning they did not fear accountability. ﴿And they denied Our signs with complete denial.﴾ al-Farra' said: this is an eloquent Yemeni dialect; they say: "kadhdhaba kidhdhāban" (he denied with denial), and "kharraqtu al-qamīṣa kharrāqan" (I tore the shirt into tearing). (Upon me is the marwa; will you ask me whether the barber or the butcher is more beloved to you?). And some of the Banu Kilab recited to me:

"Indeed, it has long hindered me from my companion, and from a need whose fulfillment is from our healing."

﴿And We have enumerated everything in a Book.﴾ ﴿So taste; for We will increase you only in punishment.﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh told me:

al-Sunni told us. Makkan. It has 770 letters, 173 words, and 40 verses.

﴿Have We not made the earth a resting-place,﴾ ﴿and the mountains as pegs,﴾ ﴿and created you in pairs,﴾ meaning kinds: males and females.

﴿And We made your sleep a rest﴾ (subat), a repose for your bodies. The sleeper is ʾmasbūt,ʾ one who does not know or perceive, as if he were dead. ﴿And We made the night a covering,﴾ a cover and veil, which clothes everything with its darkness. ﴿And We made the day a means of livelihood,﴾ a cause of your sustenance and of attending to your affairs. He named it thus, as in the saying of the poet:

"The one afflicted with worries, when worries gather around him, [the darkness of] night is his pillow, and he does not sleep."

Thus he made the pillow the thing that does not sleep, while the meaning refers to the owner of the pillow.

﴿And We built above you seven strong ones,﴾ ﴿and We made a blazing lamp,﴾ meaning shining, luminous, burning, hot, which is the sun. ﴿And We sent down from the rain-laden clouds﴾ (al-muʿṣirāt). [[Al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi: 3/364.]]

The historian said: al-muʿṣirāt means "those possessing whirlwinds" (dhawāt al-aʿāṣīr). Abu al-ʿAliya, al-Rabiʿ and al-Dahhak said: they are the clouds which bring rain but have not yet rained, like a woman who is "muʿṣir," whose menstruation is near. Abu al-Najm said:

"She has begun to menstruate, or her time of it has drawn near."

This is also the narration of al-Wali from Ibn ʿAbbas. Al-Mubarrad said: al-muʿṣirāt means "al-fāṭirāt" (those that split open). ﴿Water pouring forth﴾ means pouring abundantly. Mujahid said: "abundant." Qatada said: "in succession, one following another." Ibn Zayd said: "much."

﴿That We may bring forth thereby grain and plants,﴾ ﴿and gardens of entwined growth,﴾ meaning gathered and intertwined, one part joined with another. Its singular, according to the grammarians of Basra, is "alaff," though this view is not strong; according to others its singular is "laff" and "lafif." It is also said that it is a plural of a plural: one says "jannah lafā" and "bint lafā" and "jinān lafā" (with the lām vowelled with a ḍammah), and then "lafā" is pluralized as "alfāf."

﴿Indeed, the Day of Decision is a fixed time,﴾ as Allah, glorified is He, promised. ﴿The Day the Trumpet is blown, and you will come forth in throngs﴾ [...] [[An illegible word in the manuscript.]],

Ibn Fanjawayh told me: Ibn Shanbah told us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Kisa'i told us: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar told us: Muhammad ibn Zuhayr told us, from Muhammad ibn al-Muhtadi, from Hanzala al-Dawri, from his father, from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib, who said: Muʿadh ibn Jabal was sitting near the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the house of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari. Muʿadh said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿The Day the Trumpet is blown, and you will come forth in throngs﴾?" He said: "Muʿadh, you have asked about a grave matter." Then he let his eyes fall, and then said: "You will be gathered in ten kinds from among my community, scattered groups. Allah, the Exalted, has separated them from the congregation of the Muslims and changed their forms. Some of them are in the forms of monkeys, some in the form of pigs, some are upside down, with their feet above and their faces below, dragged upon them. Some are blind, wandering about; some are deaf and mute, who do not understand. Some chew their tongues while they hang upon their chests, and pus flows from their mouths, which the people of the gathering find disgusting. Some have their hands and feet cut off. Some are crucified on trunks of fire. Some are more foul-smelling than carrion. Some wear garments of tar, sticking to their skins. As for those in the form of monkeys, they are the tale-bearers among people, meaning the slanderers. Those in the form of pigs are those who consume forbidden gain. Those who are upside down with their faces down are the consumers of usury. The blind are those who act unjustly in judgment. The deaf and mute are those who are self-admiring in their deeds. Those who chew their tongues are the scholars and storytellers whose words contradicted their deeds. Those whose hands and feet are cut off are those who harm their neighbors. Those crucified on trunks of fire are those who inform on people to the authorities. Those more foul than carrion are those who indulge in desires and pleasures and withhold the right of Allah, the Exalted, from their wealth. Those who wear the garments are the people of arrogance, pride and vanity."" [86] [[Al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/307.]]

﴿And the sky will be opened,﴾ the people of Kufa read it with the lightened form (takhfif), and others with the intensified form (tashdid). ﴿And it will become gates,﴾ meaning it will be split open for the descent of the angels. "We were like the boon companions of Judhayma for an age of time, until it was said they would never separate."

The scholars differed concerning the meaning of ḥuqb. Some said it is a term for a period of time and an age, without a fixed limit. Abu al-Duha narrated from Ibn Masʿud, who said: "No one knows the number of the ages except Allah, Mighty and Majestic." Others said it has a limit. Then they differed about the length of its duration. Tariq ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman said: An old man called me between al-Safa and al-Marwa, and with him was a book of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr: "Abiding therein for ages"; a ḥuqb is eighty years, each day of which is a thousand years.

Ibn Fanjawayh told me: Musa ibn Muhammad and Ibn Hasan told us: Muhammad ibn ʿImran told us: Ibn al-Muqri and Abu ʿUbayd Allah told us: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-ʿUrni told us, from Sufyan, from ʿAmmar al-Dahni, who said: ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said to Hilal al-Hajari: "What do they find concerning the ḥuqb in the revealed Book of Allah?" He said: "He finds in the Book of Allah eighty years, each year twelve months, each month thirty days, each day a thousand years."

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: one ḥuqb is seventeen thousand years. He said: this verse is abrogated by ﴿so We will increase you only in punishment﴾ [[Qur'an 78:30.]], meaning that the count has ended and eternity has been attained. Some scholars said the meaning of the verse ﴿abiding therein for ages﴾ is: they will not taste during those ages anything except boiling water and ghassaq, and then they will remain for ages tasting the heat of the boiling water. Ghassaq is among the kinds of punishment. Thus it is a specification of kinds of punishment, not a specification of their staying in the Fire.

﴿They will not taste therein any coolness﴾ that would cool them from the heat, ﴿except boiling water and ghassaq﴾, which is zamharir (extreme cold). It is also said: the pus of the people of the blaze. al-Thumali said: their tears. Shahr ibn Hawshab said: ghassaq is a valley in the Fire, containing three hundred and thirty ravines, each ravine containing three hundred and thirty houses, each house having four corners, and in each corner a serpent greater than the greatest creature Allah has created, and on the head of each serpent is poison.

"If you wish, I will forbid women other than you, and if you wish, I will not taste sweet cool water, nor coolness."

Al-Hasan and ʿAta' said: ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness﴾ means refreshment and rest.

Ibn Fanjawayh told me: Musa ibn Muhammad and Ibn Hasan told us: Muhammad ibn ʿImran told us: Ibn al-Muqri and Abu ʿUbayd Allah told us: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-ʿUrni told us, from Sufyan, from ʿAmmar al-Dahni, who said: ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said to Hilal al-Hajari: "What do they find concerning the ḥuqb in the revealed Book of Allah?" He said: "He finds in the Book of Allah eighty years, each year twelve months, each month thirty days, each day a thousand years."

Ibn Fanjawayh told me: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fatḥ told us: Abu Hamid Muhammad ibn Harun al-Hadrami told us: Ziyad ibn Abi Yazid told us: Sulayman ibn Muslim told us, from Sulayman al-Hatmi, from Nafiʿ, from [Ibn ʿUmar], from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "By Allah, no one who enters the Fire will leave it until they have remained in it for ages. [87] [[Al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/308.]]

Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: It has reached me that a ḥuqb is three hundred years, each year three hundred and sixty days, each day a thousand years. Rather He said: ﴿abiding therein for ages.﴾ By Allah, it is only that when one age passes, another begins, then another, and another, and so on to everlasting eternity. He said: this verse is abrogated by ﴿so We will increase you only in punishment﴾ [[Qur'an 78:30.]], meaning that the count has ended and eternity has been attained. ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness﴾ that would cool them from the heat, ﴿except boiling water and ghassaq﴾, which is zamharir (extreme cold). It is also said: the pus of the people of the blaze. al-Thumali said: their tears. He said: "Muʿadh, you have asked about a grave matter." Then he let his eyes fall, and then said: "You will be gathered in ten kinds from among my community, scattered groups. Some are blind, wandering about; some are deaf and mute, who do not understand. Some chew their tongues while they hang upon their chests, and pus flows from their mouths, which the people of the gathering find disgusting. Some have their hands and feet cut off. Some are crucified on trunks of fire. Some are more foul-smelling than carrion. Some wear garments of tar, sticking to their skins. As for those in the form of monkeys, they are the tale-bearers among people, meaning the slanderers. Those in the form of pigs are those who consume forbidden gain. Those who chew their tongues are the scholars and storytellers whose words contradicted their deeds. Those whose hands and feet are cut off are those who harm their neighbors. Those crucified on trunks of fire are those who inform on people to the authorities. Those more foul than carrion are those who indulge in desires and pleasures and withhold the right of Allah, the Exalted, from their wealth. Those who wear the garments are the people of arrogance, pride and vanity."" [86] [[Al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/307.]]

Its singular, according to the grammarians of Basra, is "alaff," though this view is not strong; according to others its singular is "laff" and "lafif." It is also said that it is a plural of a plural: one says "jannah lafā" and "bint lafā" and "jinān lafā" (with the lām vowelled with a ḍammah), and then "lafā" is pluralized as "alfāf."

﴿Indeed, the Day of Decision is a fixed time,﴾ as Allah, glorified is He, promised. ﴿The Day the Trumpet is blown, and you will come forth in throngs﴾ [...] [[An illegible word in the manuscript.]],

Ibn Fanjawayh told me: Ibn Shanbah told us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Kisa'i told us: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Jabbar told us: Muhammad ibn Zuhayr told us, from Muhammad ibn al-Muhtadi, from Hanzala al-Dawri, from his father, from al-Bara' ibn ʿAzib, who said: Muʿadh ibn Jabal was sitting near the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the house of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari. Muʿadh said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you say about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿The Day the Trumpet is blown, and you will come forth in throngs﴾?" He said: "Muʿadh, you have asked about a grave matter." Then he let his eyes fall, and then said: "You will be gathered in ten kinds from among my community, scattered groups. Allah, the Exalted, has separated them from the congregation of the Muslims and changed their forms. Some of them are in the forms of monkeys, some in the form of pigs, some are upside down, with their feet above and their faces below, dragged upon them. Some are blind, wandering about; some are deaf and mute, who do not understand. Some chew their tongues while they hang upon their chests, and pus flows from their mouths, which the people of the gathering find disgusting. Some have their hands and feet cut off. Some are crucified on trunks of fire. Some are more foul-smelling than carrion. Some wear garments of tar, sticking to their skins. As for those in the form of monkeys, they are the tale-bearers among people, meaning the slanderers. Those in the form of pigs are those who consume forbidden gain. Those who are upside down with their faces down are the consumers of usury. The blind are those who act unjustly in judgment. The deaf and mute are those who are self-admiring in their deeds. Those who chew their tongues are the scholars and storytellers whose words contradicted their deeds. Those whose hands and feet are cut off are those who harm their neighbors. Those crucified on trunks of fire are those who inform on people to the authorities. Those more foul than carrion are those who indulge in desires and pleasures and withhold the right of Allah, the Exalted, from their wealth. Those who wear the garments are the people of arrogance, pride and vanity."" [86] [[Al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/307.]]

﴿And the sky will be opened,﴾ the people of Kufa read it with the lightened form (takhfif), and others with the intensified form (tashdid). ﴿And it will become gates,﴾ meaning it will be split open for the descent of the angels. It is also said: it will be split until it becomes like gates in pieces. It is also said: it will dissolve and scatter until gates and paths appear in it. It is also said: every servant has two doors in the heaven: a door for his deeds and a door for his provision. When the Resurrection comes, the doors will be opened.

﴿And the mountains will be set in motion﴾ away from the surface of the earth, ﴿and they will become a mirage,﴾ like a mirage. ﴿Indeed, Hell has been ever-lying in wait,﴾ a path and a passage, so there is no way to Paradise until one passes through the Fire. Muqatil said: a place of confinement. ﴿For the transgressors, a place of return,﴾ for the disbelievers. ﴿Abiding therein for ages﴾ (lābithīna). The majority read it with an alif, while ʿAlqama and Hamza read it as "labithīn" without the alif, and both are dialectal forms. ﴿Therein, ages (aḥqāban)﴾, the plural of "ḥuqb," and "ḥuqb" is the plural of "ḥuqba," as in the saying of Mutammim:

"We were like the boon companions of Judhayma for an age of time, until it was said they would never separate."

The scholars differed concerning the meaning of ḥuqb. Some said it is a term for a period of time and an age, without a fixed limit. Abu al-Duha narrated from Ibn Masʿud, who said: "No one knows the number of the ages except Allah, Mighty and Majestic." Others said it has a limit. Then they differed about the length of its duration. Tariq ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman said: An old man called me between al-Safa and al-Marwa, and with him was a book of ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr: "Abiding therein for ages"; a ḥuqb is eighty years, each day of which is a thousand years.

Ibn Fanjawayh told me: Musa ibn Muhammad and Ibn Hasan told us: Muhammad ibn ʿImran told us: Ibn al-Muqri and Abu ʿUbayd Allah told us: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-ʿUrni told us, from Sufyan, from ʿAmmar al-Dahni, who said: ʿAli ibn Abi Talib said to Hilal al-Hajari: "What do they find concerning the ḥuqb in the revealed Book of Allah?" He said: "He finds in the Book of Allah eighty years, each year twelve months, each month thirty days, each day a thousand years."

Ibn Fanjawayh told me: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Fatḥ told us: Abu Hamid Muhammad ibn Harun al-Hadrami told us: Ziyad ibn Abi Yazid told us: Sulayman ibn Muslim told us, from Sulayman al-Hatmi, from Nafiʿ, from [Ibn ʿUmar], from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "By Allah, no one who enters the Fire will leave it until they have remained in it for ages. A ḥuqb is eighty-some years, and a year is three hundred and sixty days, each day a thousand years, of what you count." So let no one rely on the hope that he will leave the Fire. [87] [[Al-Durr al-Manthur: 6/308.]]

Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: It has reached me that a ḥuqb is three hundred years, each year three hundred and sixty days, each day a thousand years. Al-Hasan said: Allah, glorified is He, has not mentioned anything without making for it a term at which it ends, but He did not make a term for the people of the Fire. Rather He said: ﴿abiding therein for ages.﴾ By Allah, it is only that when one age passes, another begins, then another, and another, and so on to everlasting eternity. There is no number for the ages except eternal abiding in the Fire. But they have mentioned that one ḥuqb is seventy thousand years, each day of which is a thousand years of what we count. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: one ḥuqb is seventeen thousand years. He said: this verse is abrogated by ﴿so We will increase you only in punishment﴾ [[Qur'an 78:30.]], meaning that the count has ended and eternity has been attained. Some scholars said the meaning of the verse ﴿abiding therein for ages﴾ is: they will not taste during those ages anything except boiling water and ghassaq, and then they will remain for ages tasting the heat of the boiling water. Ghassaq is among the kinds of punishment. Thus it is a specification of kinds of punishment, not a specification of their staying in the Fire.

﴿They will not taste therein any coolness﴾ that would cool them from the heat, ﴿except boiling water and ghassaq﴾, which is zamharir (extreme cold). It is also said: the pus of the people of the blaze. al-Thumali said: their tears. Shahr ibn Hawshab said: ghassaq is a valley in the Fire, containing three hundred and thirty ravines, each ravine containing three hundred and thirty houses, each house having four corners, and in each corner a serpent greater than the greatest creature Allah has created, and on the head of each serpent is poison.

﴿Nor any drink that quenches,﴾ from thirst, ﴿except boiling water.﴾ ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid told me: Hamid ibn Muhammad told us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hammad told us: Muhammad ibn ʿAli al-Hasan al-Shaqiqi told us: I asked Abu Muʿadh al-Nahwi, al-Fadl ibn Khalid al-Marwazi, about His saying: ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness﴾, and he said: "The coolness (barad) is sleep." Al-Kisa'i and Abu ʿUbayda said the same, and they recited concerning it:

"Its lips grew cool upon me, so it turned me away from it, and from its kisses the coolness."

The Arabs say: "The coolness prevented the coolness," meaning sleep removed the coolness. Al-Farra' said: sleep does indeed cool its owner, and the thirsty one sleeps and his thirst is cooled, so sleep is called "barad" for this reason. A poet said:

"If you wish, I will forbid women other than you, and if you wish, I will not taste sweet cool water, nor coolness."

Al-Hasan and ʿAta' said: ﴿They will not taste therein any coolness﴾ means refreshment and rest.

﴿As a recompense﴾ is in the accusative as an infinitive; its meaning is: We recompensed them with a recompense.

﴿Fitting (wifāqan)﴾, suited to their deeds as a fitting measure, as we say: "He fought a fight (qatal)," according to al-Akhfash. al-Farra' said: it is the plural of "wafq," and "wafq" and "lafq" are the same. al-Rabiʿ said: a recompense according to their deeds. al-Dahhak said: according to the measure of their deeds. Muqatil said: the punishment matched the sin, for there is no sin greater than polytheism and no punishment greater than the Fire. al-Hasan and ʿIkrima said: their deeds were evil, so Allah recompensed them with what would grieve them.

﴿Indeed they did not expect a reckoning,﴾ meaning they did not fear accountability. ﴿And they denied Our signs with complete denial.﴾ al-Farra' said: this is an eloquent Yemeni dialect; they say: "kadhdhaba kidhdhāban" (he denied with denial), and "kharraqtu al-qamīṣa kharrāqan" (I tore the shirt into tearing). In their dialect, every form of "fa''ala" has the masdar "fa''āl" with the doubled consonant. He said: a Bedouin of them said to me: "ʿAlayya al-marwa, tastaftīnī al-ḥallāq ahabb ilayka am al-qaṣṣāb?" (Upon me is the marwa; will you ask me whether the barber or the butcher is more beloved to you?). And some of the Banu Kilab recited to me:

"Indeed, it has long hindered me from my companion, and from a need whose fulfillment is from our healing."

﴿And We have enumerated everything in a Book.﴾ ﴿So taste; for We will increase you only in punishment.﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh told me:

al-Sunni told us. He said: Ibn Manjawayh informed me: Abu Dawud al-Harrani told us: Shuʿayb ibn Hayyan told us: Mahdi ibn Maymun told us: I heard al-Hasan ibn Dinar ask al-Hasan about the most severe verse in the Qur'an for the people of the Fire. Al-Hasan said: I asked Abu Barza al-Aslami, and he said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said:

"﴿So taste; for We will increase you only in punishment.﴾"

Surely for the God-fearing is a fulfilment (fawz) and deliverance from the Fire into Paradise. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak said: a place of recreation (mutanazzah).

Gardens and vineyards, and maidens with swelling breasts (kawa'ib, sing. kA'ib: a girl whose breasts have become firm and round), of equal age. Bishr ibn Abi Hazim said:

[How many a noble mare have we acquired, and [how many] a maiden whose breasts are firm, who does not know what hardship is, a pampered one.] [A line dropped from the manuscript; we have restored it from the Tafsir of al-Qurtubi: 19/183.]

Equal in age (atrab, mustawiyat fi al-sinn). And a overflowing cup (ka's dihaq). Al-Hasan, Ibn 'Abbas, Qatada and Ibn Zayd said: full and brimming. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: continuous, one after another.

They will hear therein no idle talk nor lying (kidhdhaban), meaning denial (takdhiban). This is the reading of the majority. Al-Kisa'i read it with a lightened consonant, and this is the reading of Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali, may Allah ennoble his face. Both are verbal nouns (masadir) of "takdhib" (denial).

Some people said: the lightened form kidhab is the verbal noun of "al-kadhiba" (lie); and it was said: it is "al-kadhb" (lying). al-A'sha said:

So I believed her and I disbelieved her... and a man benefits from his lying.

He lightened it here because it is not restricted by a verb that would make it a verbal noun of it, whereas he doubled the consonant in His words: "and they denied Our signs with complete denial (kidhdhaban)", because "kadhdhabu" restricts the kidhdhab by the verbal noun. [In al-Qurtubi's Tafsir (19/184): "it restricts the verbal noun by kidhdhab".]

A recompense from your Lord, a gift in full measure (hisaban): abundant, sufficient, adequate. It is said: "ahsabtu fulanan," meaning I gave him what suffices him, until he says "hasbi" (enough for me). The poet said:

We nurse the child of the tribe if he is hungry, and we give him enough (nuhsibuhu) if he is not hungry.

That is, He gives him until he says "hasbi."

It was also said: a recompense according to their deeds. Abu Hashim read "'ataa'an hisaban" with a fatha on the ha' and a shadda on the sin, on the pattern fa''al, meaning sufficient (kaffafan). Al-Asma'i said: the Arabs say "hassabtu al-rajul" with the shadda when one honours him, and he recited:

When his guest comes to him, he honours him, with milk gathered in the waterskin or fresh milk he milks for him.

[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 10/246.]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Ibn Habish related to us: al-Tahrani related to us: Yahya ibn al-Fadl informed us: Wahb ibn 'Umar related to us: Harun ibn Musa informed us, from Hanzala, from Shahr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he read "'ataa'an hasanan" with the nun.

Lord of the heavens and the earth and what is between them, the Most Merciful (al-Rahman). Ibn Mas'ud, al-Ashhab, Abu Ja'far, Shayba, Nafi' and Abu 'Amr, Salam and Ya'qub read rabbi and al-rahmani with the ra' and the nun in the nominative (raf'). Ibn 'Amir, 'Isa and 'Asim read both in the genitive (khafdan), and this was chosen by Abu Hatim. Ibn Kathir, Muhayis, Yahya, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read rabbi in the genitive and al-Rahmanu in the nominative, and this was chosen by Abu 'Ubayd, who said: this is the most balanced reading in my view, that the first of them be in the genitive because of its proximity to His words "a recompense from your Lord," so that it is an adjective (na't) of it, and that al-Rahmanu be in the nominative because of its distance from it.

They will not be able to address Him (la yamlikuna minhu khitaban): speech. Al-Kalbi said: intercession, except by His permission.

On the day when the Spirit (al-Ruh) stands, they differed concerning it.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Ibn Kharija related to us: 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Abbas al-Tayalisi related to us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah related to us: my father related to us: Ibrahim ibn Tahman related to us, from Muslim al-A'war, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A group of Jews came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "Tell us about the Spirit, what is it?" He said: "It is an army of the armies of Allah, not angels, having heads and hands and feet, and they eat food." Then he recited: "On the day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows..." and said: "These are an army, and these are an army." [88] [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 19/187.]

Ibn 'Abbas said: it is the greatest of the angels in creation. Ibn Fanjawayh informed us: Musa related to us: Ibn 'Alawiyya related to us: Isma'il related to us: al-Musayyab related to us: Thabit Abu Hamza related to us, from 'Amir, from 'Alqama, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Spirit is an angel greater than the heavens and the mountains and greater than the angels; he is in the fourth heaven, glorifying twelve glorifications every day, from each glorification He creates an angel; he will come on the Day of Resurrection in a row by himself. Al-Sha'bi and al-Dahhak said: he is Jibril. Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Indeed, to the right of the Throne is a river of light, like the seven heavens, the seven earths and the seven seas; Jibril (peace be upon him) enters it every dawn and bathes, and his light increases upon his light, his beauty upon his beauty, and his greatness upon his greatness. Then he shakes himself, and Allah the Glorified brings forth from every drop that falls from his feathers so-and-so-many thousands of angels; there enter each day seventy thousand angels into the Bayt al-Ma'mur in the Ka'ba, and they do not return to it until the Hour is established. Wahb said: Jibril stands before Allah the Glorified with his limbs trembling; Allah creates from every tremor a thousand angels. So the angels are in rows before Allah with their heads bowed; when Allah permits them to speak, they say: "There is no god but You," and this is His saying: "On the day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows."

They will not speak except one whom the Most Merciful permits, and he says what is right (sawaban), meaning: there is no god but Allah. Mujahid said: they are a creation in the form of the children of Adam, eating and drinking. Abu Salih said: a creation resembling people but not people. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: they are the children of Adam. Qatada said: and this is what Ibn 'Abbas used to conceal. Ibn Mujahid related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Spirit is a creation of Allah, and He fashioned them in the forms of the children of Adam, and no angel descends from heaven without being accompanied by one of the Spirit. 'Atiyya said: they are the spirits of people, who stand with the angels between the two blasts, before the spirits are returned to the bodies. Ibn Zayd said: my father used to say: it is the Qur'an, and he recited: "And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command" [Surah al-Shura: 52].

On the day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows. Al-Sha'bi said: they are the two ranks of the Lord of the worlds on the Day of Resurrection: a rank of the Spirit and a rank of the angels. "They will not speak except one whom the Most Merciful permits, and he says what is right": he says: there is no god but Allah, in this world.

That is the true Day; so whoever wills, let him take a return (ma'ab) to his Lord, a refuge and a path to His obedience.

"Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment" (inna anzarnakum 'adhaban qariban).

It means the Resurrection; and it was said: the killing at Badr.

"On the day when a man sees what his hands have sent forth, and the disbeliever says: 'Would that I were dust!'"

'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the earth will be stretched like a hide, and the beasts, cattle and wild animals will be gathered; then retribution will be made among the animals, until the hornless sheep is avenged against the horned one that gored it. When He has finished the retribution, He will say to them: "Be dust!" Then the disbeliever says: "Would that I were dust!"

Mujahid said: on the Day of Resurrection, retribution is taken for the hornless one from the one that gored it. Al-Muqatil said: Allah the Glorified and Exalted gathers the beasts, the creeping things and the birds, every creature except the two weighty ones (jinn and men), and says: "Who is your Lord?" They say: "The Most Merciful, the Compassionate." Then the Lord, blessed and exalted, says to them after He has judged between them, until He has avenged the hornless against the horned: "I created you and subjected you to the children of Adam, and you were obedient during your lives; now return to that which you were; be dust!" and they become dust. When the disbeliever looks at any thing that has become dust, he wishes and says: "Would that I had been in the world in the form of a pig, with my provision like its provision, and today in the Hereafter I were dust." 'Ikrima said: It has reached me that when the beasts, wild animals and cattle see the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection and the grief and sorrow they are in, they say: "Praise be to Allah who did not make us like you: there is no Paradise we hope for, nor a Fire we fear."

And 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us: Muhammad ibn Khalid informed us: Dawud ibn Sulayman related to us: 'Abd ibn Humayd related to us: al-Hasan ibn Musa related to us: Ya'qub ibn 'Abd Allah related to us: Ja'far related to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Dhakwan Abu al-Zinad, who said: When judgment has been passed among people, and the people of Paradise are ordered to Paradise and the people of the Fire to the Fire, it is said to the rest of the nations and to the believers among the jinn: "Return to dust!" and they return to dust. At that point the disbeliever, seeing them having returned to dust, says: "Would that I were dust!"

Laith ibn Sulaym also said this: the believing jinn return to dust. 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz said: the believing jinn are around Paradise in its outskirts and open spaces, but they are not within it.

I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Jubayr say: I saw in some tafsirs that the disbeliever here is Iblis, because he blamed Adam for being created from clay and boasted that he was created from fire. When on the Day of Resurrection he beholds what Adam and his believing children have of reward, rest and mercy, and sees what he and his people have of severity and punishment, he wishes he were in Adam's place, and then says: "Would that I were dust!"

Abu Hurayra said: then the dust will say to the disbeliever: "No, and no honour for you, you who made me like yourself."

Surely for the God-fearing is a fulfilment (fawz) and deliverance from the Fire into Paradise. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak said: a place of recreation (mutanazzah).

Gardens and vineyards, and maidens with swelling breasts (kawa'ib, sing. kA'ib: a girl whose breasts have become firm and round), of equal age. Bishr ibn Abi Hazim said:

They say: "The Most Merciful, the Compassionate." Then the Lord, blessed and exalted, says to them after He has judged between them, until He has avenged the hornless against the horned: "I created you and subjected you to the children of Adam, and you were obedient during your lives; now return to that which you were; be dust!" and they become dust. 'Ikrima said: It has reached me that when the beasts, wild animals and cattle see the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection and the grief and sorrow they are in, they say: "Praise be to Allah who did not make us like you: there is no Paradise we hope for, nor a Fire we fear."

Laith ibn Sulaym also said this: the believing jinn return to dust. 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz said: the believing jinn are around Paradise in its outskirts and open spaces, but they are not within it.

Then he shakes himself, and Allah the Glorified brings forth from every drop that falls from his feathers so-and-so-many thousands of angels; there enter each day seventy thousand angels into the Bayt al-Ma'mur in the Ka'ba, and they do not return to it until the Hour is established. Wahb said: Jibril stands before Allah the Glorified with his limbs trembling; Allah creates from every tremor a thousand angels. So the angels are in rows before Allah with their heads bowed; when Allah permits them to speak, they say: "There is no god but You," and this is His saying: "On the day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows."

They will not speak except one whom the Most Merciful permits, and he says what is right (sawaban), meaning: there is no god but Allah. Mujahid said: they are a creation in the form of the children of Adam, eating and drinking. Abu Salih said: a creation resembling people but not people. Al-Hasan and Qatada said: they are the children of Adam. Qatada said: and this is what Ibn 'Abbas used to conceal. Ibn Mujahid related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Spirit is a creation of Allah, and He fashioned them in the forms of the children of Adam, and no angel descends from heaven without being accompanied by one of the Spirit. 'Atiyya said: they are the spirits of people, who stand with the angels between the two blasts, before the spirits are returned to the bodies. Ibn Zayd said: my father used to say: it is the Qur'an, and he recited: "And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command" [Surah al-Shura: 52].

On the day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows. Al-Sha'bi said: they are the two ranks of the Lord of the worlds on the Day of Resurrection: a rank of the Spirit and a rank of the angels. "They will not speak except one whom the Most Merciful permits, and he says what is right": he says: there is no god but Allah, in this world.

That is the true Day; so whoever wills, let him take a return (ma'ab) to his Lord, a refuge and a path to His obedience.

"Indeed, We have warned you of a near punishment" (inna anzarnakum 'adhaban qariban).

It means the Resurrection; and it was said: the killing at Badr.

"On the day when a man sees what his hands have sent forth, and the disbeliever says: 'Would that I were dust!'"

'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, the earth will be stretched like a hide, and the beasts, cattle and wild animals will be gathered; then retribution will be made among the animals, until the hornless sheep is avenged against the horned one that gored it. When He has finished the retribution, He will say to them: "Be dust!" Then the disbeliever says: "Would that I were dust!"

Mujahid said: on the Day of Resurrection, retribution is taken for the hornless one from the one that gored it. Al-Muqatil said: Allah the Glorified and Exalted gathers the beasts, the creeping things and the birds, every creature except the two weighty ones (jinn and men), and says: "Who is your Lord?" They say: "The Most Merciful, the Compassionate." Then the Lord, blessed and exalted, says to them after He has judged between them, until He has avenged the hornless against the horned: "I created you and subjected you to the children of Adam, and you were obedient during your lives; now return to that which you were; be dust!" and they become dust. When the disbeliever looks at any thing that has become dust, he wishes and says: "Would that I had been in the world in the form of a pig, with my provision like its provision, and today in the Hereafter I were dust." 'Ikrima said: It has reached me that when the beasts, wild animals and cattle see the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection and the grief and sorrow they are in, they say: "Praise be to Allah who did not make us like you: there is no Paradise we hope for, nor a Fire we fear."

And 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us: Muhammad ibn Khalid informed us: Dawud ibn Sulayman related to us: 'Abd ibn Humayd related to us: al-Hasan ibn Musa related to us: Ya'qub ibn 'Abd Allah related to us: Ja'far related to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Dhakwan Abu al-Zinad, who said: When judgment has been passed among people, and the people of Paradise are ordered to Paradise and the people of the Fire to the Fire, it is said to the rest of the nations and to the believers among the jinn: "Return to dust!" and they return to dust. At that point the disbeliever, seeing them having returned to dust, says: "Would that I were dust!"

Laith ibn Sulaym also said this: the believing jinn return to dust. 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz said: the believing jinn are around Paradise in its outskirts and open spaces, but they are not within it.

I heard Abu al-Qasim ibn Jubayr say: I saw in some tafsirs that the disbeliever here is Iblis, because he blamed Adam for being created from clay and boasted that he was created from fire. When on the Day of Resurrection he beholds what Adam and his believing children have of reward, rest and mercy, and sees what he and his people have of severity and punishment, he wishes he were in Adam's place, and then says: "Would that I were dust!"

Abu Hurayra said: then the dust will say to the disbeliever: "No, and no honour for you, you who made me like yourself."
